Feature: Interrupts can be generated based on negative edge detection at GPIO input
Test Description: Verify negative-edge interrupt behavior on GPIO inputs for randomly selected pads and ensure interrupt status is set and cleared correctly.
Remarks: Requires system interrupt enable for the selected GPIO block. Uses a flag to synchronize the interrupt handler. Stimulus is applied via a memory-mapped interface. Pads are selected randomly without repetition.
Test Steps / Procedure:
1) Enable the system interrupt for the targeted GPIO block in the system register.
2) Enable the platform interrupt controller line for the selected GPIO block.
3) Initialize the stimulus memory location to the default high value.
4) For each unique pad in the target range, configure the per-pin control register for input with negative-edge interrupt.
5) Enable the corresponding bit in the GPIO group interrupt enable register for the selected pad.
6) Drive the input to generate a falling edge using the stimulus interface, then restore it to the default state.
7) Wait until the interrupt handler clears the pending flag.
8) In the handler, read the per-pin register and verify the input state and raw interrupt indicator.
9) Read the GPIO group interrupt status register and verify the bit for the selected pad is set.
10) Disable the corresponding bit in the GPIO group interrupt enable register and clear the per-pin interrupt through the per-pin control register.
11) Verify the per-pin status indicates the interrupt is cleared and the GPIO group interrupt status register is cleared.
12) Clear the system raw status bit in the system register and verify it is cleared.
13) Clear the platform interrupt controller line and repeat for all selected pads.
Validation / Acceptance Criteria:
1) GPIO input state indicates the expected value after the event → Pass if the input state bit is set as expected.
2) GPIO raw interrupt bit is asserted after the falling edge → Pass if the per-pin raw interrupt indicator is set.
3) GPIO group interrupt status reflects the selected pad → Pass if the corresponding group status bit is set.
4) After clearing, the per-pin interrupt status is cleared → Pass if the per-pin status indicates cleared.
5) After clearing, the GPIO group interrupt status is zero → Pass if the group status register reads as cleared.
6) System raw status bit for the GPIO interrupt is cleared → Pass if the system status bit reads as cleared.
7) No unexpected "Interrupt Not occurred" path is taken → Pass if no error increments occur and the test error counter remains zero at finish.

Remarks: Uses compile-time selection for the GPIO instance. Synchronizes main and ISR using a shared flag. Stimulus transitions are applied through a memory-mapped location. Per-pin interrupt is cleared by a defined write sequence.

12) Clear the system raw status for the GPIO interrupt and clear the interrupt controller line.
13) Repeat the sequence for all pad indices.

1) Input status after the event → Pass if the input state bit indicates the expected value.
2) Raw interrupt after the falling edge → Pass if the per-pin raw interrupt indicator is set.
3) Group interrupt status → Pass if the corresponding bit for the active pad is set.
4) Per-pin interrupt clear → Pass if the per-pin readback matches the expected cleared value.
5) Group interrupt clear → Pass if the group status register reads as cleared.
6) System raw status clear and IRQ line → Pass if the system status is cleared and the line is acknowledged.
